As of April 2026, the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) is temporarily suspending employer contributions to the Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS) to conserve cash amid a severe financial crisis, threatening to run out of funds within 12 months. The move, effective April 10, aims to save approximately $2.5 billion through September 30 by pausing $200 million in biweekly payments, but officials state there is no immediate impact on current or future retirees. Key Details of the Pension Suspension Action Taken: USPS is halting its employer contributions to the FERS defined benefit plan. Continued Payments: USPS will continue to transmit employee contributions to FERS, as well as contributions to the Thrift Savings Plan (TSP) and Social Security. Financial Context: The agency reported $118 billion in net losses since 2007, with quarterly losses reaching $1.25 billion in early 2026. Past Precedent: The Postal Service previously suspended these payments in 2011 during a similar financial crisis. Postal Retirement System Background Plan Types: Career employees are covered under FERS or the older Civil Service Retirement System (CSRS). Funding Mechanism: Unlike other federal agencies that receive appropriations, USPS must fund its retirement obligations through its own operating revenue. Unfunded Liabilities: All three retirement-related funds (including health benefits) have unfunded liabilities. For more context on the historical challenges of these funds, see this USPS OIG report.
